question: Does the dual reading of a gauge law's allowed states succeed exactly on planar graphs, and do local parity laws written on no graph, with non-degenerate knot matroids, carry graphs?

definitions.planar by embeddings: some rotation system (a cyclic order of the neighbours at every vertex) gives V - E + F = 2; decided by exhaustive search, independent of any matroid
definitions.local law, three of size six: random parity constraints of size six with every variable in exactly three constraints (m/2 constraints on m variables)
definitions.local law, sparse: m/2 random parity constraints on m variables, each of a random size from three to five

public_inputs.graphs: K4, K5, K6 (planar search capped; known non-planar), wheels W4-W9, prisms on 3-6 sides, the cube, the octahedron, K3,3, K3,4, the Petersen graph, and 24 random 3-connected cubic graphs on 8, 10 and 12 vertices
public_inputs.local laws: 40 laws of each kind on 12, 14 and 16 variables (240 laws)
public_inputs.ledrappier: x(i,j)+x(i+1,j)+x(i,j+1)=0 on L x L tori for L = 3..8

forbidden_inputs: the planarity search never uses the matroid; the readings never see the presentation

predictions.T1: for every 3-connected graph whose planarity search terminates, the dual reading of its gauge law's allowed states succeeds exactly when it is planar
predictions.T2: among the local laws whose knot matroid is 3-connected, at most 5 percent are graphic or cographic, and at least 20 local laws are 3-connected

primary_observable: per graph: planarity by embeddings, dual reading; per local law: dimension, dual dimension, 3-connectivity, graphic, cographic; per torus: dimension of Ledrappier's allowed states
cheapest_meaningful_control: (C1) the planarity search accepts the known planar graphs (wheels, prisms, cube, octahedron) and rejects K5, K3,3 and Petersen; (C2) a graph law presented with every variable in exactly two constraints (a disguised graph) is recovered by the reading
independent_check: check_result.py re-runs the planarity search with a different vertex order, recomputes allowed codes, readings and 3-connectivity with its own linear algebra, and recounts
decision_or_followup_rule: A signal is T1 and T2 holding. A non-planar graph with a successful dual reading, or graphic local laws well above 5 percent, becomes the subject of ticket B.
first_executable_signal: KNOT-SPACE-20261020-001A-E001: the dual reading succeeded on all 21 labelled-planar graphs, failed on all 12 genuinely non-planar ones, and succeeded on 6 random cubic graphs later found planar by a rotation-system search
stop_rule: Stop after the declared roster or budget.
nonclaims: Finite enumeration only; the general statements belong to ticket B.
Graphicness is decided completely only for 3-connected knot matroids.
No claim about native structure, distance, physical space or dimension.
